source_review.notes: Reviewed Okasaki's primary thesis and functional red-black paper, Adams's weight-balanced sets paper, Princeton's VFA/Appel red-black verification materials, the AFP root-balanced proof, and current official Clojure PersistentTreeMap and Haskell containers Data.Map sources. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked tree/node, comparator, in-order map, height, size, AVL balance, red-black color/black height, changed frontier, join/split, reachability, and identity notation.
Checked set/map, version/map/node/entry identity, binary/page trees, and logical/structural serialization remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: All complexity statements name their balance/operation assumptions or are explicitly conditional.

evidence: Recomputed versions v0-v7, including the 30,20,10 right rotation and the v3 branch at key 5.
Recomputed v5 keys 10,20,25,30,40; v6 keys 5,10,20,30; v5 height three; and old/new key-30 values thirty/THIRTY.
Recomputed all stored size/height fields and selected shared identities for the finite tuple trees.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Finite node/height results are not allocator-byte or production-cost measurements.

evidence: Verified path-copy persistence inductively from private replacement nodes and immutable reused subtrees.
Verified right rotation preserves in-order sequence A,y,B,z,C and requires bottom-up metadata reconstruction.
Verified AVL height gives logarithmic point work/allocation under constant comparator/metadata assumptions and that red-black/weight/treap claims require their own invariants.
Verified join/split preconditions partition key ranges and that durable child-before-root publication is separate from in-memory immutability.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Insertion, deletion, join/split, persistence, lifetime, concurrency, and durability are separate proof obligations.

evidence: Reviewed empty, duplicate/no-op/replacement, every insertion rotation, absent/root/leaf/one/two-child deletion, successor extraction, sorted/reverse keys, and branches from every root.

Reviewed mutable/stateful/nontransitive comparators and keys, expensive payload/aggregates, size/height overflow, recursive depth, allocation failure, refcount cycles/destruction, arenas, and stalled readers.
Reviewed CAS loss/retry/ABA, cancellation, hostile graph IDs/cycles/depth, schema/comparator migration, crash publication, root pinning, quotas, authorization, and sharing leakage.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Resource controls cover roots/readers, depth/nodes/bytes, comparator/aggregate time, diff/range/output, history, and serialized graphs.

evidence: The executable independently checks strict lower/upper BST bounds, exact height and size, and AVL balance at every node of every retained version.
It checks old-root values, branch isolation, rotation results, replacement isolation, and expected sharing of untouched subtrees.
The chapter specifies separate red-black/weight, join/split, lifetime, publication, serialization, and storage validators.
invariant_checking.notes: The executable covers persistent AVL insertion/replacement only; it is not evidence for deletion or other balance families.

evidence: Reviewed ordered-map/comparator/value semantics, functional AVL construction/rotations, functional red-black framing, deletion frontier, and balance-family trade-offs.
Reviewed augmentation, join/split/bulk algebra, identity/iterators/diff, reclamation/failure, concurrency/parallelism, and serialization/durability.
Reviewed security/resource controls, independent-model/invariant/sharing evidence, fault/concurrency tests, and benchmark dimensions.
proof_review.notes: Published verified algorithms are cited; the chapter does not claim to reproduce their complete proofs.

evidence: Abstraction, persistence, metadata, AVL, red-black, complexity, join/split, and lifetime/publication arguments state separate assumptions.
Deletion and size-sensitive bulk bounds are explicitly conditional on exact family algorithms.
The finite AVL trace explicitly disclaims deletion, other families, reclamation, concurrency, storage, security, and performance proof.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No balancing family is claimed universally superior.

evidence: The standard-library-only Python trace passed exact thirteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under Python 3.14.4.
It emits evidence=finite_persistent_avl_version_trace and reproduces rotation, branching, lookup, metadata, balance, persistence, and selected sharing.
All eight final external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local links passed draft module validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No deletion, red-black/weight/treap, join/split, bulk parallelism, allocation fault, reclamation, CAS, serialization, crash, hostile input, or production performance was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Progresses from ordered-map semantics through immutable AVL/red-black repair, balance families, augmentation and bulk operations, then identity, lifecycle, concurrency, storage, and evidence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed comparator/key/value ownership, smart constructors, deletion frontiers, cached metadata, iterators/diffs, roots/readers/retention, allocation failure, GC/refcount/arenas, CAS publication, parallel cancellation, logical/graph formats, child-before-root durability, GC, migrations, quotas, faults, and tail metrics.

pedagogical_review.notes: Builds on Level I balance families and prior persistence modules, includes a reproduced branching AVL trace, ten distinct worked examples, and five graduate exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Okasaki, Adams, Appel/VFA, Nipkow/AFP, Clojure, Haskell containers, AVL/red-black/weight-balanced/treap, security, performance, reliability, storage, formal-methods, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite insertion trace prove neither arbitrary persistent trees, deletion, red-black/weight/treap/rebuild algorithms, join/split/bulk bounds, mutable-payload isolation, comparator/key safety, fixed-width/allocation/failure safety, refcount/GC/epoch/arena correctness, thread safety/linearizability/progress, graph serialization, durable pages/MVCC/crash recovery/GC, hostile-input security, production memory/cache/GC/tail behavior, certification, nor deployment fitness.
